caption_used: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.

The plot illustrates the performance of different knowledge editing methods on a biomedical language model, displaying accuracy as a function of co-occurrence number. The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic scale, ranging from 1 to 10^3, with tick labels at 1, 10, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” and has a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 65, with tick labels at 5-unit intervals. There are six data series, each represented by a line with distinct markers. The “Base” model is represented by a black line with circular markers, starting at approximately 39% accuracy at a co-occurrence number of 1 and increasing to approximately 44% at a co-occurrence number of 10^3. The “MEND” model is shown as a brown line with diamond markers, beginning at approximately 45% and rising to approximately 56% at a co-occurrence number of 10^3. The “FT” model is a blue line with triangular markers, starting at approximately 42% and reaching approximately 48% at a co-occurrence number of 10^3. The “IKE” model is represented by a red line with plus markers, starting at approximately 44% and increasing to approximately 52% at a co-occurrence number of 10^3. The “MEMIT” model is a green line with square markers, beginning at approximately 50% and rising to approximately 55% at a co-occurrence number of 10^3. Finally, the “ROME” model is shown as a dark green line with x markers, starting at approximately 51% and increasing to approximately 66% at a co-occurrence number of 10^3.
